children: The Reserve Bank of India likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Thursday, four traders said, as the rupee fell past the 96-per-dollar mark for the first time in over a month after the U.S. Federal Reserve hiked rates.
was at 96.08 per dollar, down 0.1% from its previous closing level.
State-run banks were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, traders said.
Persistent central bank intervention has supported the rupee in the face of multiple headwinds ranging from higher oil prices to elevated global bond yields.

The central bank also likely conducted dollar-rupee sell/buy swaps for mid-tenor maturities, persisting with forward market interventions intended to drain excess rupee liquidity from the banking system, traders said.
The excess liquidity has declined to its lowest level since August 31 following tax payments and the RBI's recent FX market interventions.
